names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Filit, cu cei patru fii ai săi»; the same site's page for his wife spells him «Filet Sincliticul».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 27 Μαρτίου, «Άγιοι Φιλητός ο Συγκλητικός, Λυδία σύζυγος αυτού, Θεοπρέπιος και Μακεδόνας τα τέκνα αυτών, Αμφιλόχιος ο Δούκας και Κρονίδης ο κομενταρήσιος οι Μάρτυρες», with the rank words left off.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 2297, «Филит Иллирийский, сенатор, мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s line declines the forename and gives no by-name at all; the province is read off the name page.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 23 марта ст. ст. — «Мчч. Филита , Лидии , супруги его, Македона , Феопрепия , Кронида и Амфилохия , чад их (117-138).»

attestations.note: The corpus kept this company on the menologion’s 27 March, off saint.gr and doxologia, and this calendar keeps it on 23 марта ст. ст. — a difference of four days, so neither a style conversion nor the same number, and `day-candidates.mjs`, which matches on the menologion number, could not see any of the six. They were found by the name sweep and by grepping the Latin stems. Each of the six has a name page of its own, 2297, 2571, 1416, 2245, 1308 and 154, every one read here, and every one gives this single day, so no second-day note is owed. **The day’s line and the page’s own life disagree about who two of the six are.** The line reads «Мчч. Филита , Лидии , супруги его, Македона , Феопрепия , Кронида и Амфилохия , чад их (117-138).», whose «чад их» sits after all four names and reads as though Cronides and Amphilochius were children of Philetus and Lydia too. The life’s own title has it otherwise — «Мученики Филит, Лидия, жена его, чада их Македон и Феопрепий, Кронид и Амфилохий», the children being Macedon and Theoprepius and the other two standing apart — and the life itself says why: Amphilochius was the «военачальник» of Illyria to whom the family was sent to be tortured, and Cronides the «начальник тюрем» who had come to believe. That is the corpus’s own reading off the Greek, so nothing in any `display_name`, `types` or relation was changed and the line is recorded here as the looser of the two. The day page carries ten hymns and not one of them is under any of these six names. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 27 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Filit, cu cei patru fii ai săi»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 27ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Φιλητός ο Συγκλητικός, Λυδία σύζυγος αυτού, Θεοπρέπιος και Μακεδόνας τα τέκνα αυτών, Αμφιλόχιος ο Δούκας και Κρονίδης ο κομενταρήσιος οι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The page names all six of the company where doxologia.ro names two, puts the persecution «(125 μ.Χ.)» under Hadrian «(117 - 138 μ.Χ.)», gives the duke's province as Slavonia, and ends by having the emperor set the survivors free so that they «τελείωσαν τον βίο τους προσευχόμενοι», ended their lives praying. Its couplet for the couple agrees with that ending — «καὶ μετ' εἰρήνης τέλος», and their end was in peace — while its couplet for the two sons says that they died. The page reconciles neither, and nothing on this folder is changed on the strength of it. No hymn is printed.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Σε καιρό διωγμού (125 μ.Χ.), και όταν αυτοκράτορας ήταν ο Αδριανός (117 - 138 μ.Χ.), ο Φιλητός με τη σύζυγο του Λυδία και τα δυο τους παιδιά, συνελήφθησαν» — the year the page gives for the persecution in which the family was seized. The same page then has the emperor set them free, so this is not recorded as a year of death.
